subject: Collaboration Commit Slate - initial GDoc and timing
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Ball <sarah.ball@novumhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 6 Oct 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Collaboration Commit Slate - initial GDoc and timing

Hi Sarah —

Great to meet last week. Per our conversation I pulled a starter slate together that frames the evaluation milestones, stakeholder owners, and a recommended 6-week close rhythm. The GDoc below is editable so you and any Novum stakeholders can add notes directly.

Quick high-level asks from our side:
- Confirm pilot success criteria (we sketched three hypotheses)
- Identify who from Novum will own the data/access items and procurement contacts
- Flag any mandatory security/compliance blockers up front so we can scope evidence requests

GDoc (editable): https://docs.google.com/document/d/1aBcD_example_collab_slate
Attachments: novum-eval-questions.pdf (list of suggested technical checks)

Proposed next steps:
1) Quick sync with your technical lead this week (30 mins)
2) Shared acceptance criteria and test dataset by next Tue
3) Procurement kickoff (contract skeleton) on or before week 2

If that timeline looks reasonable I can loop in Jordan to schedule the demo and Marissa to own the acceptance checklist.

Thanks —
Irene Choi
Senior Solutions Manager, Redwood Inference
irene.choi@redwood.com | (415) 555-0148

From: Sarah Ball <sarah.ball@novumhealth.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@novumhealth.com>, procurement@novumhealth.com
Date: Mon, 6 Oct 2025 12:44:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Collaboration Commit Slate - initial GDoc and timing

Hi Irene —

Thanks for pulling this. I reviewed the slate quickly and it looks helpful. A few clarifications from my side:

- The acceptance criteria look good but we need an explicit performance target for 95th-percentile latency (our clinical UX team asked). Can you add a recommended latency SLO for the pilot?
- Procurement prefers a short-list of required deliverables for the contract (SLA, data handling, termination data return). I copied Liam and procurement so they can weigh in.
- Our security team will want to review the novum-eval-questions.pdf — do you have a single contact who can triage and return answers?

Proposed availability for the technical sync: Wed 10/08 11:00–11:30 ET or Thu 10/09 14:00–14:30 ET. Let me know which works.

Best,
Sarah
Director of Clinical Product, Novum Health

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Ball <sarah.ball@novumhealth.com>, Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@novumhealth.com>, procurement@novumhealth.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 6 Oct 2025 13:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Collaboration Commit Slate - initial GDoc and timing

Thanks Sarah — great notes. Replying with owners: 

- Latency SLO: Karthik will add recommended targets to the GDoc (we typically propose a 95th-percentile target of ~500ms for the pilot at 1k rps equivalent workload, then tighten for prod).
- Procurement deliverables: Jordan will share the skeleton contract highlights (SLA, data handling, termination/export, indemnities).
- Security triage: Marissa will be primary contact for the novum security team and will coordinate answers and evidence.

Sarah — Wed 10/08 11:00 ET works for us. Jordan will send a calendar invite.

Attaching a short checklist I use for the first acceptance draft; I'll also add inline comments to the GDoc.

Thanks,
Irene

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Ball <sarah.ball@novumhealth.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 7 Oct 2025 08:17:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Collaboration Commit Slate - initial GDoc and timing

Hi Sarah —

I took a quick pass on the novum-eval-questions.pdf and added a short evidence matrix in the GDoc (access control, data retention, audit logs). The doc has a comment tagging your security lead — if they prefer a spreadsheet format I can export.

On the latency SLO: Karthik, can you confirm the pilot recommendation so I can lock the language?

Also, procurement — high level ask: can you share standard lead times on PO/contract review so we can align the 6-week rhythm? A typical procurement window we see from customers is 2–3 weeks for initial review, but we want to map it into the timeline.

Thanks —
Marissa
Senior Trust & Compliance Partner, Redwood Inference

From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@novumhealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Sarah Ball <sarah.ball@novumhealth.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@novumhealth.com
Date: Thu, 9 Oct 2025 11:03:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Collaboration Commit Slate - initial GDoc and timing

Thanks everyone — appreciate the clear slate. A few procurement notes:

- We can aim for a 3-week procurement review if we have the contract skeleton and the security evidence tied to specific sections.
- Please include a simple SOW appendix listing the pilot deliverables (we need that to create the internal PO).
- We also need clarity on data residency for any logs exported during the pilot — our policy requires EU/US segmentation for patient-adjacent data; Novum will own the dataset and controls.

I reviewed the GDoc and left a couple comments tagging Jordan for the SOW language. If Redwood can produce a short SOW appendix and an evidence index by Mon 10/13, procurement can target a PO by week of 10/20.

Liam
Sr. Procurement Manager, Novum Health
liam.oconnor@novumhealth.com

On Wed, Oct 8, 2025 at 11:00 AM Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com> wrote:
> Confirming the 11:00 ET sync — calendar invite sent.
>
> Irene
